The numbers below are the benchmark results committed in `benchmarks/`. They are one run on one machine, and the files do not record which machine, so read them as orders of magnitude and relative costs, not as a promise about your hardware. Pull requests are not judged against them (see [Regression gate](#regression-gate)).

## Rust core (criterion)

`benchmarks/latest_benchmarks.json`: 7 benchmarks, collected on 2026-02-07 at commit [`8135e47`](https://github.com/Open-Quant/openquant/commit/8135e47). Times are criterion's mean per iteration with its 95% confidence interval.

`benchmarks/baseline_benchmarks.json` holds the same numbers: the baseline was last refreshed from this run.

Benchmarks that exist in `crates/openquant/benches/` but are not in `benchmarks/benchmark_manifest.json`, so are neither committed here nor gated: `hpc_parallel/serial_linear` (hpc_parallel_scaling.rs), `hpc_parallel/threaded_linear` (hpc_parallel_scaling.rs), `hpc_parallel/threaded_nested` (hpc_parallel_scaling.rs), `streaming_hpc/scaling/*` (streaming_hpc_scaling.rs). Run them with `cargo bench -p openquant --bench <file stem>`.

## Python data layer

`benchmarks/data_processing/latest.json`, written by `python/benchmarks/benchmark_data_processing.py`: 4 symbols × 100,000 rows (400,000 rows), 5 iterations per function. The file records neither a date nor a commit. `just py-bench-data` regenerates it (with 200,000 rows per symbol, not the size committed here).

| Function | Rows | Mean (ms) | p95 (ms) | Rows/s | MB/s |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `clean_ohlcv` | 400,000 | 431.8 | 430.2 | 926,317 | 48.2 |
| `data_quality_report` | 400,000 | 202.2 | 205.0 | 1,977,855 | 102.8 |
| `align_calendar` | 400,000 | 487.7 | 485.1 | 820,180 | 49.2 |
| `load_ohlcv_csv` | 400,000 | 234.6 | 235.6 | 1,704,667 | 120.3 |
| `load_ohlcv_parquet` | 400,000 | 458.7 | 468.5 | 872,087 | 4.9 |

There is no committed `benchmarks/data_processing/baseline.json`, so `just py-bench-data-compare` has nothing to compare against until one is made, and no CI job runs these benchmarks.

## Regression gate

`.github/workflows/benchmark-regression.yml` runs on pull requests that touch `crates/openquant/`, the workspace manifests, the toolchain pin or the benchmark scripts. It builds the pull request's merge base and its head, runs the `perf_hotspots` and `synthetic_ticker_pipeline` benches on both **on the same runner**, and fails if a benchmark's mean slowed down by more than 35% (`scripts/check_bench_thresholds.py`), or by more than its entry in `benchmarks/threshold_overrides.json`. A benchmark that stops producing a result fails the gate too. Comparing base and head back to back removes the machine-to-machine variation that made a gate against the committed baseline fail on unrelated changes. Because the workflow is path-filtered, it is not suitable as a required status check.

| Benchmark | Allowed slowdown |
| --- | ---: |
| `structural_breaks_get_sadf_sm_power` | 35% |
| `bet_sizing_bet_size_reserve_fit` | 35% |
| `bet_sizing_bet_size_reserve_reuse_fit` | 55% |
| `synthetic_ticker_ewma_100k` | 35% |
| `synthetic_ticker_risk_metrics_var_es_cdar` | 35% |
| `synthetic_ticker_seq_bootstrap_2k_600` | 35% |
| `synthetic_ticker_pipeline_end_to_end` | 50% |

## Reproduce

```bash
just bench-all      # cargo bench -p openquant --bench perf_hotspots --bench synthetic_ticker_pipeline
just bench-collect  # target/criterion -> benchmarks/latest_benchmarks.json (manifest only)
just bench-check    # latest vs the committed baseline, with the thresholds CI uses
just py-bench-data  # Python data-layer benchmarks -> benchmarks/data_processing/latest.json
python3 scripts/docs/generate_site_pages.py --write   # re-render this page
```

Refresh `benchmarks/baseline_benchmarks.json` only in a pull request that says why; a slowdown and a new baseline in the same change hides the slowdown.
